claim_scope: a mean latency below the deadline can hide a deadline miss in a fixed tail sample
stale observations, deadline misses, invalid actions, bounds violations, expired chunks, and excessive uncertainty need distinct gate reasons
uncertainty thresholds trade accepted coverage against failure risk and failure capture in a fixed labeled fixture
equal mean, percentile, maximum, and miss-rate summaries can hide different consecutive deadline-miss bursts
an asynchronous schedule must distinguish stale queued actions from queue underflow, and fallback recovery needs explicit hysteresis
a fixed negative control separates healthy-input hysteresis from explicit policy-reactivation authorization
authored lifecycle reports keep request, operation, success, timeout or failure, and reactivation authorization distinct
a fixed reactivation-receipt audit rejects stale, future, misbound, unauthorized, denied, replayed, consumed, and out-of-order records
equal coverage, accepted failure rate, and count-based rejection recall can hide which authored-severity failure remains accepted
actions inside identical static bounds can differ under a per-field physical-unit adjacent-step delta gate, which fails closed without bound applied-action history
current and prior actions must share schema, frame, field, unit, rate, clock, command, acknowledgement, session, boot, and step identity before a transition is compared
within one authored executor epoch, an exact command retry returns a cached receipt while payload conflicts, stale order, and session or boot mismatches remain distinct

code.config: standard-library deadline gate with the Chapter 15/21 shared mobile-base-v1 action schema

data.name: procedural latency bursts, physical-unit action packets, epoch-bound idempotency, adjacent-step transitions, async chunks, and fallback transitions

limitations: six hand-authored latency values rather than measured wall-clock timings

fallback labels, authored lifecycle reports, timeout thresholds, and hand-authored reactivation inputs are not actuator commands, reachability checks, completion-detector evidence, operator availability, backup-MRM switching, or safety proofs

receipt identity, approver, run, target, time, and sequence fields are authored strings or integers with in-memory single-session state; they provide no authentication, signature, integrity, revocation, reboot persistence, concurrency guarantee, or authorization-system validation
the discrete async schedule does not measure a scheduler, clock, network, queue implementation, or chunk fusion

uncertainty scores, failure labels, and unvalidated consequence proxy weights are hand-authored and do not validate an estimator, calibrated probability, injury level, monetary loss, or real-world risk

the adjacent-step action audit shares an authored physical-unit schema and checks identity fields, but its acknowledgement and step history remain hand-authored; it does not authenticate actuator feedback, compute physical acceleration or jerk, or establish feasibility, tracking stability, or safety
the immutable command ledger is in-memory teaching state; it does not provide durable transactions, concurrent linearization, crash recovery, authenticated receipts, or exactly-once physical effects
no scheduler, network, ROS, model, accelerator, hardware, fault tree, or certification
